title: Horizon and Monsoon
premise: Riverboat captain Quentin Ashgrove agrees to ferry a dying prospector, Elias Vane, upriver in exchange for a map to the forbidden headwaters — and a promise to deliver it to Vane's estranged daughter. But the map is also wanted by the Meridian Company, whose private enforcers murdered Vane's partners to bury evidence that the source valley sits on land stolen from a displaced river community. Pursued by Company gunboats and racing the monsoon season, Quentin must choose between his lifelong rule of never stopping and never belonging, and the justice the law will never deliver. In the flooded climax at the source, he exposes the Company's forged land deeds to the daughter and the valley's surviving elders, then burns the map so no one can own what the monsoon reclaims.
about_author: Kestrel Vasquez spent a decade working seasonal river freight before turning to writing full-time, and her fiction is known for its granular knowledge of water, weather, and the people who live by both. She lives half the year aboard a restored sternwheeler with her dog, Barge.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. He pilots the Marguerite through low-water shoals, establishing his skill and his creed: keep moving, owe no one. A debt collector reminds him why stopping costs more. Emotional beat: restless self-sufficiency masking old grief.

chapters.title: A Passenger at Dusk
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A feverish stranger, Elias Vane, begs passage upstream past the licensed limit, offering a folded oilskin packet as payment. Quentin refuses; Vane collapses on the dock. Emotional beat: reluctance cracking into reluctant compassion.

chapters.title: The Prospector's Bargain
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Vane, dying, trades the map for two promises: carry him toward the source, and give the packet to his daughter, Sera Vane, in Port Calloway. Quentin accepts only the delivery. Emotional beat: a promise made too easily.

chapters.title: Company Men
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Grey-coated Meridian Company agents board asking after a 'thief of survey documents.' Quentin lies smoothly and feels the first hook of trouble set. Emotional beat: fear disguised as charm.

chapters.title: Last Words on the Levee
chapters.summary: Vane's POV, rendered as Quentin later recalls it. Vane dies at dawn describing the source valley and the men who killed his partners. His last word is his daughter's name. Emotional beat: the weight of inherited guilt transferring to Quentin.

chapters.title: Port Calloway
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. He finds Sera Vane working a salvage yard; she wants nothing from the father who abandoned her. Quentin leaves the packet unopened against her wishes. Emotional beat: anger meeting an obligation it cannot refuse.

chapters.title: The Unopened Packet
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Alone, she opens the oilskin: the map, a journal naming Meridian's forgeries, and a letter she reads three times. She catches Quentin before he casts off. Emotional beat: grief converting to purpose.

chapters.title: Terms of Passage
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Sera buys passage not to the source but to the county records office downriver, where the original deeds are kept. They argue about justice versus survival. Emotional beat: two creeds colliding on one deck.

chapters.title: Records and Ruin
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The records annex has burned — recently, and not by accident. A clerk whispers that Meridian's surveyor, Aldous Crane, signed the fire permit himself. Emotional beat: the law revealed as the obstacle.

chapters.title: Gunboat Wake
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A Meridian gunboat shadows the Marguerite through the narrows. Quentin uses a sandbar trick to slip it, but knows they're marked now. Emotional beat: thrill curdling into dread.

chapters.title: What the Journal Says
chapters.summary: Shared scene, alternating close POV. By lamplight they read Vane's journal: the source valley was home to the Riverkin community, removed by forged deeds so Meridian could dam the headwaters. Emotional beat: inheritance reframed as theft.

chapters.title: The Informant
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. An old deckhand, Tomas, admits he once ran supplies for Meridian's removal crews and can guide them past the checkpoints. Quentin doesn't trust him. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance over shared shame.

chapters.title: Monsoon Warnings
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Radio reports put the monsoon making landfall in nineteen days; the upper river will be unnavigable after. He sets a hard deadline and hates that he cares whether they make it. Emotional beat: commitment arriving uninvited.

chapters.title: Checkpoint at Stone Latch
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Meridian inspectors search the boat; Sera hides the map inside a coffin being shipped upriver. Quentin's smooth lying frays. Emotional beat: terror managed with craft.

chapters.title: Tomas's Confession
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. He tells Sera about the night the Riverkin were driven out — the burning of their ferry landing, the children on the far bank. Emotional beat: guilt seeking absolution it may not deserve.

chapters.title: Crane Boards
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Surveyor Aldous Crane comes aboard under polite flag, offering Quentin money for the map and hinting he knows about the coffin. Quentin declines without blinking. Emotional beat: predator recognizing predator.

chapters.title: Dead Calm Above the Falls
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Below the great falls, the engine fails — sabotaged, Quentin discovers, while they were at checkpoint. Stranded, exposed, they repair under watchful hills. Emotional beat: vulnerability forcing honesty between them.

chapters.title: Night Fishing, Night Talking
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Waiting for parts, Quentin tells Sera about the brother he couldn't save by always moving on; she tells him about the father she stopped waiting for. Emotional beat: two loners mapping each other.

chapters.title: The Riverkin Ferryman
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A hidden Riverkin pilot, Odessa, offers to take them above the falls through channels no chart shows — if they swear the valley stays unowned. Emotional beat: trust extended as a test.

chapters.title: Portage of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Hauling the Marguerite's essentials through abandoned Riverkin paths, they find carved names on the rocks — including Vane's, from before his exile. Emotional beat: Sera seeing her father whole for the first time.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Weir
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Tomas signals a waiting Meridian launch; Crane's men seize the map case. But Sera had already split the documents — Tomas led them to a decoy. Emotional beat: betrayal met with quiet preparation.

chapters.title: What Tomas Chose
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Cornered by Crane, Tomas realizes the Company plans to kill witnesses this time, not just displace them. He turns his signal lantern the other way. Emotional beat: redemption bought at the edge of a gun.

chapters.title: Running the Flooded Gorge
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Pre-monsoon swells turn the gorge lethal; Odessa pilots while Quentin runs the valves. They survive by inches. Emotional beat: mastery and humility fused in white water.

chapters.title: Crane's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Crane's POV. Over a hail-speaker, Crane offers amnesty for the map and promises the valley will be 'developed humanely.' Sera answers with her father's journal read aloud. Emotional beat: defiance as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Valley Appears
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Through lifting rain they see the source basin — terraced, overgrown, unmistakably once inhabited. Sera understands what was taken. Emotional beat: awe braided with fury.

chapters.title: Elders of the Headwaters
chapters.summary: Odessa's POV. The surviving Riverkin elders receive the strangers warily; some want the outsiders gone. Odessa vouches for them. Emotional beat: hospitality extended across old wounds.

chapters.title: Reading the Land
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The elders show him the old stone weirs that prove continuous ownership predating every deed. Quentin, a man of charts, learns to read water as testimony. Emotional beat: a skeptic converted by evidence.

chapters.title: Fifteen Days of Rain
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter. Monsoon arrives early; the camp digs in, repairs the weir, and waits out a week of storm. Bonds deepen; Tomas earns his keep hauling stone. Emotional beat: community as shelter.

chapters.title: Crane Ascends
chapters.summary: Crane's POV. Crane leads armed crews upriver, gambling the monsoon won't stop him. His own survey notes begin to unsettle him — the forgeries are his signature too. Emotional beat: ambition hollowing into panic.

chapters.title: The First Skirmish
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Meridian scouts probe the valley mouth; the defenders use floodwater and the weir to strand their boats without bloodshed. Emotional beat: victory that feels like a countdown.

chapters.title: Sera's Decision
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera proposes taking the journal and deed copies to the circuit judge at Fort Amity — outside the law's reach only until they bring the law itself. Quentin argues it's a trap. Emotional beat: hope risking everything.

chapters.title: Downriver in the Storm
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin and Sera run the flooded river to Fort Amity through wreckage and lightning, the Marguerite nearly lost. Emotional beat: love acknowledged in the teeth of the storm.

chapters.title: The Judge Who Owes Meridian
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Judge Harrow listens, then reveals Meridian holds his debts. He stalls. Sera realizes the law here is rented, not owned. Emotional beat: despair sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Public Reading
chapters.summary: Ensemble. Rather than petition quietly, Sera reads Vane's journal aloud in the fort square as the storm breaks; river folk gather, many with their own removal stories. Emotional beat: private truth becoming public force.

chapters.title: Harrow's Choice
chapters.summary: Judge Harrow's POV. Facing the crowd and his own ledger, Harrow issues a stay on all Meridian titles pending federal review — and resigns his Company debt publicly. Emotional beat: a compromised man choosing a side.

chapters.title: Crane at the Source
chapters.summary: Crane's POV. Crane reaches the valley anyway, orders the weir blown, and watches the flood he unleashes threaten his own crews. Quentin's crew rescues them. Emotional beat: power drowning in its own consequences.

chapters.title: The Burning of the Map
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. With deeds voided and the valley's existence now public knowledge, Quentin burns the map before the elders, the judge, and Crane: no one will own the source, ever. Emotional beat: release of the thing he carried.

chapters.title: What Stopping Costs
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin surveys the Marguerite's damage and, for the first time, considers staying through the dry season to help rebuild the ferry landing. Emotional beat: a moving man learning the price of staying is worth paying.

chapters.title: Daughter of the Headwaters
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera buries her father's letter at the carved rocks beside his name, adding her own beneath it. Odessa names her keeper of the valley's records. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed and transformed.

chapters.title: Horizon and Monsoon
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, closing. The rains end; the river drops; boats move again. Quentin takes the Marguerite downriver with Sera aboard — going somewhere, for once, rather than away. Emotional beat: arrival as a new kind of departure.
